title: Permutation Difference between Two Strings
statement:
You get two strings `s` and `t`. No letter occurs twice in `s`, and `t` is a rearrangement of `s`: it holds exactly the same letters, each once. So every letter has one index in `s` and one index in `t`, both counted from 0.

For each letter, take the absolute difference between its index in `s` and its index in `t`. Return the sum of these differences over all letters; this sum is called the permutation difference of `s` and `t`.
constraints: No character appears more than once in s
t is a permutation of s
s contains only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

Because no letter repeats, each letter has exactly one index in `s` and one in `t`, and the answer only needs the pair of indices for every letter. Scanning `t` for each letter of `s` works but repeats the same search over and over (O(n²)). Recording once where every letter of `s` sits, in a hash map, turns each search into a single lookup.

## Approach

1. Walk through `s` and store each letter's index `i` in the map `indexInS`.
2. Walk through `t` with index `j`, and look up `i`, the index of the same letter in `s`.
3. Add `|i - j|` to `difference`.
4. After the last letter of `t`, every letter has been counted exactly once: return `difference`.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "abc"` gives `indexInS = {a: 0, b: 1, c: 2}`. Then `t = "bac"`: at `j = 0` the letter is `b` with `i = 1`, so `difference = 1`; at `j = 1` the letter `a` has `i = 0`, adding 1 more for `2`; at `j = 2` the letter `c` has `i = 2` and adds 0. The answer is `2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass over each string, and every map operation is O(1).
- Space: O(n) for the map, which never holds more than 26 letters.

## Pitfalls

- Take the absolute value: letters move both left and right, and signed gaps would cancel to 0 on every input.
- Measure both indices from 0 in the same way; the difference is only meaningful between positions counted alike.
- `t.indexOf(letter)` inside a loop gives the same total, but costs a full scan per letter; the map is the pattern that scales.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `indexInS` | map from each letter to its index in `s` |
| `i` | an index in `s` (in the second loop, where letter `t[j]` sits in `s`) |
| `j` | the current index in `t` |
| `difference` | running sum of the index gaps |

narration.3: Create the map from each letter to its index in s.
narration.4: Visit every index of s once.
narration.5: Record where letter s[i] sits; letters never repeat, so nothing is overwritten.
narration.7: The sum of the gaps starts at zero.
narration.8: Now visit every index j of t.
narration.9: Look up i, the index in s of the same letter, in constant time.
narration.10: Add the distance between the two positions; Math.abs keeps it non-negative.
narration.12: Every letter was counted exactly once; return the total.
